s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss and eye pain with signs of intraocular inflammation
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius
Blood and urine cultures, electrocardiogram, and echocardiogram were unremarkable

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Infectious endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain and culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, consistent with infectious endophthalmitis

shortlist.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, a specific type of streptococcal infection

shortlist.label: Actinomycotic endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain showed gram-positive rods in a branching pattern, suggestive of Actinomyces

shortlist.label: Polymicrobial bacterial iris abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Mixed flora on Gram stain and presence of gram-positive cocci and rods

shortlist.label: Streptococcal iris abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, and clinical presentation is consistent with an iris abscess

raw.rationale: The presence of gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern on Gram stain, along with the culture revealing Streptococcus intermedius, suggests a polymicrobial infection. The clinical presentation of a focal granuloma at the pupillary margin and the development of hypopyon also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infectious endophthalmitis
rejected.why: While the patient has an infection, the focal nature of the granuloma and the lack of posterior segment involvement suggest a more localized process.

rejected.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
rejected.why: The presence of gram-positive rods on Gram stain suggests a polymicrobial infection, not just a streptococcal one.

rejected.label: Actinomycotic endophthalmitis
rejected.why: Although the Gram stain shows gram-positive rods, the culture did not specifically identify Actinomyces, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with a polymicrobial bacterial iris abscess.

rejected.label: Streptococcal iris abscess
rejected.why: The presence of gram-positive rods on Gram stain suggests a polymicrobial infection, not just a streptococcal one.
